cifar100_hierarchical_classification.description: CIFAR-100 hierarchical classification (paper Table 2 and Table 4 CIFAR-100 columns) on the paper's 5-level CIFAR hierarchy, scored on the 10,000 official test images.

accuracy.description: Fine-label top-1 accuracy (%), the paper's no-loss-in-recognition constraint.

top5_accuracy.description: Fine-label top-5 accuracy (%); the true class should stay near the top of the ranked list.

coarse_accuracy.description: Accuracy (%) of the submitted prediction at the level just above the leaves (20 nodes).

path_consistency.description: Percentage of examples whose submitted multi-level predictions (all four non-leaf levels) are exactly the ancestors of the submitted top-1 leaf, i.e. a valid tree path.

ms.description: Mistake severity: mean LCA distance between true and top-1 class over misclassified examples.

ahd@1.description: Mean LCA distance of the top-1 prediction over all examples.

ahd@5.description: Permutation-invariant top-5 hierarchy distance used as a complementary severity check.

ahd@20.description: Permutation-invariant top-20 hierarchy distance used as a broad ranked-list severity check.

hops.description: Paper's headline hierarchy-aware ranking metric over the full class order.

hops@5.description: Hierarchy-aware preference score restricted to the top five ranked classes.

hops@20.description: Hierarchy-aware preference score restricted to the top twenty ranked classes.

fpa.description: Full-path accuracy (%): the top-1 leaf and the submitted prediction at every non-leaf level are all correct.

cifar100_hierarchical_classification.setup_note: Paper protocol kept: WRN-28-8, 100 epochs, 45K train / 5K val split of the CIFAR-100 training set, 10K official test set. Paper numbers below are 5-seed means; the gym's reference is a single seed (seed 7). The paper reports CE FPA only in the text (77.11). macro_accuracy was dropped because both splits are exactly class-balanced, where it equals accuracy; fine_coarse_consistency was generalised to path_consistency over all four non-leaf levels (the paper's hierarchical-consistency property).
